source: Response exponent for the spinner, giving finer control at low speed. The curve is anchored at 64 units per poll: below that an exponent above 1.00 attenuates, at and above it movement passes through unchanged. A higher exponent therefore makes the spinner SLOWER overall -- raise Rotary Sensitivity to get the top speed back.

A higher exponent therefore makes the spinner SLOWER overall -- raise Rotary Sensitivity to get the top speed back.

source: Stick positions within this many ADC counts of centre (127 = full deflection) read as exactly centred. The rest of the travel is rescaled so the response is smooth at the edge and full deflection still reads full scale.
effective_source: Stick positions within this many ADC counts of centre (127 = full deflection) read as exactly centred. The rest of the travel is rescaled so the response is smooth at the edge and full deflection still reads full scale.

source: As Analog Controller Dead Zone (X), for the Y axis (pitch, or accelerator/brake on the driving controller).
effective_source: As Analog Controller Dead Zone (X), for the Y axis (pitch, or accelerator/brake on the driving controller).

source: Subtracts a constant (in ADC counts) from every X sample, in host orientation before any device convention. Cancels a stick that rests off-centre; a centred stick is moved by it, which is the point.
effective_source: Subtracts a constant (in ADC counts) from every X sample, in host orientation before any device convention. Cancels a stick that rests off-centre; a centred stick is moved by it, which is the point.

source: As Analog Controller Offset (X), for the Y axis.
effective_source: As Analog Controller Offset (X), for the Y axis.

source: Response exponent for the X axis, anchored at full deflection: an exponent above 1.00 gives finer control near centre while full deflection still reads full scale. Unlike the mouse/rotary curves this costs no top speed, so there is no paired sensitivity control.
effective_source: Response exponent for the X axis, anchored at full deflection: an exponent above 1.00 gives finer control near centre while full deflection still reads full scale. Unlike the mouse/rotary curves this costs no top speed, so there is no paired sensitivity control.

source: As Analog Controller Response Curve (X), for the Y axis.
effective_source: As Analog Controller Response Curve (X), for the Y axis.

source: Map Jaguar numpad 0-9, * and # to keyboard keys. 'Number Row Keys' will use 1234567890-= keys, 'Keypad Keys' will use 0123456789/* keypad keys.
effective_source: Map Jaguar numpad 0-9, * and # to keyboard keys. 'Number Row Keys' will use 1234567890-= keys, 'Keypad Keys' will use 0123456789/* keypad keys.

source: Scales mouse movement before it is converted to quadrature pulses. The emulated device can only emit one pulse per controller poll, so raising this past what the game's poll rate can carry adds lag rather than speed.
effective_source: Scales mouse movement before it is converted to quadrature pulses. The emulated device can only emit one pulse per controller poll, so raising this past what the game's poll rate can carry adds lag rather than speed.

source: Discards horizontal mouse movement at or below this many host units per poll. A noise gate for a jittery source (or an analog stick mapped to the mouse); a real mouse reports nothing at rest and needs none. Movement above the threshold passes at full size -- the dead zone drops samples, it does not shrink them.

Movement above the threshold passes at full size -- the dead zone drops samples, it does not shrink them.

source: As Mouse Dead Zone (X), for vertical movement.
effective_source: As Mouse Dead Zone (X), for vertical movement.

source: Subtracts a constant from every horizontal sample. Cancels a source that reports a small non-zero movement while at rest -- typically an analog stick mapped to the mouse, which otherwise drifts forever. A real mouse reports exactly zero at rest and is unaffected.
effective_source: Subtracts a constant from every horizontal sample. Cancels a source that reports a small non-zero movement while at rest -- typically an analog stick mapped to the mouse, which otherwise drifts forever. A real mouse reports exactly zero at rest and is unaffected.

source: As Mouse Offset (X), for vertical movement.
effective_source: As Mouse Offset (X), for vertical movement.

source: Response exponent for horizontal movement, giving finer control at low speed. The curve is anchored at 64 units per poll: below that an exponent above 1.00 attenuates, at and above it movement passes through unchanged. Because ordinary movement is well below 64 units, a higher exponent makes the mouse SLOWER overall -- raise Mouse Sensitivity to get the top speed back. These are two different controls.

source: As Mouse Response Curve (X), for vertical movement.

source: Logging and watchdog aids for troubleshooting and bug reports.
effective_source: Logging and watchdog aids for troubleshooting and bug reports.

source: Lightweight runtime watchdog that logs GPU/DSP PC escape, GPU/DSP wedge, and video stall events to the RetroArch log. Helpful when filing bug reports about games that hang or go to a black screen mid-play. Verbose mode also dumps a state heartbeat every 10 seconds.

source: How 16-bit source tiles are rendered in their preview PNGs. The blitter cannot know whether 16-bit values are CRY or RGB16 -- that is display-time interpretation -- so this only changes the preview image, never the tile's hash. 'Both' writes a -cry and a -rgb PNG per tile.
